credits.title: Credits and sources
credits.body:
The Great Trek is a family game about the 1837 trek north from Grahamstown. The families in it are invented. The places, prices and most events come from period sources: Captain W. Cornwallis Harris's Wild Sports of Southern Africa (1839), James Backhouse's Narrative (1844), Andrew Steedman's Wanderings (1835) and many modern histories. Press H in an event to read the history behind it.

Code: C17 with SDL3, SDL3_ttf and SDL3_image (zlib licence) and cJSON (MIT). Font: VT323 (SIL Open Font Licence). The game is free software under the GNU GPL v3. See CREDITS.md and docs/planning for every source.
side.title: Which family will you play?
side.dutch.about: Frontier farmers leaving the Colony with their herds. Little money but many cattle and sheep. The trekker laagers welcome you and you have a voice in their council. English officials and missionaries are cooler toward you.
side.english.about: Families of the 1820 Settlers going north to trade, hunt or farm. More money and colonial credit, cheaper goods in the Colony, but the trekkers are suspicious of you, and you must earn their trust before they let you into their laager.

orders.title: Trek options
orders.medicine.auto: Give it to anyone who falls ill
orders.medicine.chosen: Give it by hand, on the party screen
orders.medicine.about: Medicine is given a dose a day to the sick while it lasts. Give it to anyone who falls ill, or give it by hand: when someone is ill, choose Give medicine beside them on the party screen (P).
orders.flock.about: Eating from the flock, as the trekkers did, means a sheep is slaughtered whenever the fresh meat runs out, about one every few days, and the wagon's meal and biltong are saved. Keeping the flock means eating the wagon's stores first and slaughtering only when they run low, so the sheep are kept for trade and wages.
orders.pace.about: A hard pace covers more ground but wears out the oxen and the people. An easy pace is gentle on everyone but slow.
orders.rations.about: Full rations keep people strong. Meagre rations make the food last longer. Starvation rations are for emergencies only.
orders.night.about: Drawing the wagon into a laager each evening costs a little time but keeps the herd and the family much safer at night. Once you have joined the trekkers' united laager, your nights are safer still. Guarding the herd is tiring but helps.
orders.sabbath.about: Resting on Sundays costs a day a week, but lifts everyone's spirits and is expected among the trekkers.

help.title: How to play
help.1: It is April 1837. Bring your family north from Grahamstown, alive, to the end of the road, or to a place you choose to stop.
help.2: Choose with the number keys, the arrow keys and Enter, or the mouse. Esc opens the menu: save and quit, this page, the glossary and the settings.
help.3: On the road, Travel on sets the wagon moving and any key stops it. From the same menu you can rest, hunt, mend the wagon, and set the trek options: pace, rations, the night watch, the sheep and the medicine.
help.4: M shows the map, J the journal and G the glossary of period words. In an event, P shows the party, S your supplies, and H the history behind it.
help.5: Buy well in Grahamstown: enough oxen for a full span and some over, a spare wheel or axle, water vats for the dry Karoo, food, powder and lead. The store shows how long your food will last and how far each journey's end is.
help.6: Listen to the people you meet. Their warnings about rivers, the dry country, fever and the fly come from what really happened.
help.7: The game saves after every step, and there is no going back. When someone dies, they are buried by the road.
